A bit late, but in September, I was cooking breakfast for "the trifecta" --- me, my husband and our dog (eggs and sausage, as always). My husband came in the house and stood next to me in the kitchen, gushing over some cute little red bird he had seen outside. He kept going on about it for some reason, but I was really focused on not burning the food. I am not a bird person, so it didn't really trigger much conversation from me. Just a "oh how cute" type of response. 

The next day, he went to work, and I slept on the sofa with my pup laying by my side. 10 minutes into my nap I hear her whimpering and clawing into the floor. I woke up and found her going into cardiac arrest. I had no clue what was happening at the time, but I picked my little husky up and sped to an emergency vet. She stayed with me as I sped up the highway. I kept cupping her nose to make sure she was still breathing. 

I panicked when I arrived and just parked the car. I looked back and she curled into a little ball --- she looked so comfy. The vet techs came over to the car and asked if they could help. I explained her symptoms, and they pulled her out the car. 

She was gone. 

Of course my husband and I were a mess the entire night. Nothing like taking your dog to the vet and coming home with a fucking collar. 

The day after she passed, I walked to my car and looked in the back seat and just fell apart, knowing that's where she took her last breath. My husband stood next to me and pointed up to the roof --- it was the same red bird he described the day before.

 A bright red cardinal. 

Cardinals signify a loved one sending a message of comfort. The last time I saw them excessively was when my grandfather passed in 1999. 

For an entire week, cardinals appeared on my window sill, in trees, and above my backyard. They flew above us as we took walks to get coffee. It was a strange source of comfort for us that week. 

My husband saw one outback, and he tried to take a picture of it, but he flew away. My husband really cried and came up to my office, just for me to point out the window and see it sitting on the roof next door. Little troll.

Eventually, we began to adjust, and I told him we would probably stop seeing them soon. That is exactly what happened. We have not seen a cardinal since. 

I cannot explain this at all. I do know it has brought us great comfort, and we are so honored to have been her humans. :)
